# Audio & video development development notes

> Building FFmpeg, H.264 decoding, capture, streaming and player integration.

## Historical context

Historical development notes from 2015–2017. Their original publication dates and source attribution are retained; translation or catalog updates do not make the examples current.
The examples were not rerun for this reorganization. Old Swift syntax, APIs, dependencies, service addresses and App Store rules may be obsolete; check current official documentation before applying them.

## Articles by original publication date

- [Integrating ijkplayer for live video on iOS](https://allluckly.cn/en/journal/2016-05-13-integrating-ijkplayer-for-live-video-on-ios/index.md): Records downloading the source, initialising dependencies, compiling FFmpeg, packaging IJKMediaFramework and adding it to an iOS project. The focus is on the role of each directory and build step in the ijkplayer integration. Originally published: 2016-05-13. Published in 2016. The scripts and project configuration correspond to the ijkplayer source used at the time. Originally credited to jianshu_wl; edited and archived by Bison.
- [Building FFmpeg-iOS on a Mac](https://allluckly.cn/en/journal/2017-07-11-building-ffmpeg-ios-on-a-mac/index.md): Records preparing gas-preprocessor and yasm on a Mac, then running the FFmpeg-iOS build script. It explains script locations, dependency installation, and output directories to prepare libraries for the later decoding examples. Originally published: 2017-07-11. Published in 2017, the build output includes Homebrew installation logs from El Capitan. Script and permission settings are retained as historical examples. Originally credited to Bison. Content is retained as published.
- [H.264 Decoding with FFmpeg-iOS](https://allluckly.cn/en/journal/2017-07-11-h-264-decoding-with-ffmpeg-ios/index.md): Starts by importing FFmpeg-iOS and configuring header search paths, then traces opening media, finding a video stream, initializing the decoder, reading packets, and releasing resources. A wrapper example brings the H.264 decoding steps together. Originally published: 2017-07-11. Published in 2017, the article uses older FFmpeg APIs, including av_register_all and avcodec_decode_video. Originally credited to Bison. Content is retained as published.
- [A Simple Streaming Wrapper for FFmpeg-iOS](https://allluckly.cn/en/journal/2017-07-12-a-simple-streaming-wrapper-for-ffmpeg-ios/index.md): Builds on the preceding FFmpeg articles to set up a local nginx streaming test environment. Server configuration, a client-side streaming wrapper, and playback in VLC connect the process of sending encoded data with checking the resulting stream. Originally published: 2017-07-12. Published in 2017, the code and local server configuration reflect the FFmpeg and nginx environments used at that time. Originally credited to Bison. Content is retained as published.
- [Camera and Microphone Capture with FFmpeg-iOS](https://allluckly.cn/en/journal/2017-07-20-camera-and-microphone-capture-with-ffmpeg-ios/index.md): First uses FFmpeg device input support to list cameras and microphones, then presents a native iOS camera-capture example. The two approaches illustrate media-device enumeration and the basic configuration of a system capture session. Originally published: 2017-07-20. Published in 2017, the device-input and capture code uses the FFmpeg and AVFoundation APIs available at that time. Originally credited to Bison. Content is retained as published.
